memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If a man has sexual relations with her and her monthly flow touches him, he will be unclean for seven days; any bed he lies on will be unclean.'" - Lev 15:24 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here the man does not get off with an evening. He carries the full seven days — the same term she carried.

Whatever else is happening in this verse, notice the principle: closeness means sharing the cost. He did not stay clean while she waited. Her season became his.

That is a picture of what love actually costs. To be genuinely close to someone is to be affected by what affects them. Their grief becomes partly your grief. Their difficulty reshapes your week. Their bad season colours yours.

We instinctively resist this. We would rather love people from a slight distance, close enough to care but far enough not to be inconvenienced. Paul calls us to something braver: rejoice with those who rejoice; mourn with those who mourn (Rom 12:15). Not observe the mourners. Mourn with them.

And this is what Christ did in full. He did not remain at a safe distance from our condition. He shared in our humanity (Heb 2:14). He took our uncleanness on Himself entirely — God made him who had no sin to be sin for us (2 Cor 5:21).

Seven days for the man in Leviticus. The cross for the Son of God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you love people from a comfortable distance?
2. Whose burden are you being invited to genuinely share?
3. What does it mean to you that Christ took your condition as His own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You that You did not love me from a distance but took my condition as Your own. Give me courage to enter into others' burdens rather than watching from outside. Amen.
